A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Swift-SVD work. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression accuracy, runtime, memory, numerical-stability, and ablation results, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on larger models, comparative serving throughput, and longer generation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same output-covariance accumulation, eigendecomposition, optimal weight projection, and dynamic rank-allocation procedure, including the same alpha grid and retention ratio. Algorithm 1 is renamed without changing its steps; LoRA integration remains future work.

E1.justification: The language-modeling and reasoning datasets remain unchanged, including ARC-Challenge already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.1. The additions concern model sizes, comparators, hardware, and generation-length settings within the retained tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds Basis Sharing and naive SVD comparisons in Tables B.2 and B.4. It also introduces SVD-LLM and Dobi-SVD comparator rows for Qwen3-4B and comparative serving throughput, substantially expanding comparator participation beyond v1's corresponding evaluations.

E3.justification: New protocols include the FP32 Basis Sharing comparison, Qwen-32B evaluation on one 80GB H800, and H800 serving experiments with uniform, dynamic, and per-type-average rank allocations. Appendix B.8 additionally compares 1024- and 8192-token generation at batch size 16 and prompt length 32. These are added settings, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.7 adds an analysis of Dobi-SVD's serving slowdown, including a control that substitutes its per-type average ranks. Appendix B.8 tests whether throughput benefits survive longer generation, and B.3 extends allocation comparisons to Qwen3-4B. The existing calibration, hyperparameter, spectral, and qualitative analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–6 and Appendix Table B.1 retain their numerical results, while v2 adds Tables B.2–B.7. New findings include Qwen-32B accuracy and baseline OOM outcomes, similar throughput among uniform methods, and lower throughput for dynamic Dobi-SVD. These are additional results under specified settings, not same-setting improvements over v1. Table B.2 also introduces averages inconsistent with its listed task scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its proof, and Equations 1–12 remain unchanged. Appendix B.8 adds a short complexity argument that fixed-dimension KV up-projection costs O(L) per decoding step and that cache bandwidth savings also scale linearly with cached length L.

C1.justification: The headline optimality, efficiency, stability, dynamic-allocation, and 3–70× compression-speedup claims remain unchanged. The conclusion adds the limited claim that Swift-SVD factors can initialize LoRA fine-tuning, explicitly leaving the resulting recovery benefits as future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial explanations of serving behavior: similar uniform ranks yield similar throughput, while Dobi-SVD's allocation is argued to increase KV-cache traffic. It also explains long-generation overhead, tentatively attributes the Qwen-32B accuracy increase to regularization, and discusses initialization quality as a possible constraint on LoRA recovery.

D1.justification: v1 promises code upon acceptance; v2 states that code is available and supplies a repository link. The new experiments also document FP32 comparison settings, the single-H800 setup, and serving batch, prompt, and output lengths. The existing software and RTX 5090 information is mostly relocated into Section 4.

R1.justification: v2 adds Basis Sharing, MoDeGPT, and Sundrani (2025), and distinguishes its joint per-matrix allocation from ShortGPT's layer removal and MoDeGPT's per-block allocation. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or citation suffixes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes include limited copyediting, Algorithm 1 renaming, hardware-description relocation, additional appendix subsections and cross-references, and new project-lead, conflict-of-interest, acknowledgements, and impact statements.

P2.justification: v2 adds six experimental tables, B.2–B.7, and redraws Figure 3 and Figure B.3 with explicit NER and importance axes and separate legends. Figure B.3(c) gains a gate series. Existing displays are reflowed, and the retained generated-response table moves from B.2 to B.8.

improvement.justification: The added serving controls, longer-generation tests, and 32B evaluation strengthen practical validation, while clearer plots and code-access information improve usability. However, new numerical reporting errors limit the gains: Table B.2 reports 0.57 average accuracy for Swift-SVD at ratio 0.8 although its seven listed scores average approximately 0.49. The additions provide a useful but qualified improvement over the retained core evidence.
